title: The Analogy of the Seed and the Body
english: Of seeds: But if it dies, it bears much fruit. It is evident that the living one dies; and you once prevented the eating of the things possessed which have life-giving power. And the apostle Paul says: That which you sow is not made alive unless it dies (1 Cor 15:36); and that which you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be born, but a naked grain if it should be wheat or something of the rest; but God gives to it a body, as He willed (1 Cor 15:37-38). It has been demonstrated also concerning the seeds, how it dies and is made alive, and that God gives to it a body, as He willed.

You have in the Old Testament that God sincerely accepted sacrifices from the righteous, and that all the saints ate meat and the rest of the creatures with thanksgiving; you were persuaded through the holy gospels that [text ends in gap].
